page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, providing 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The server includes 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a compute-tailored 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features also integrate 1800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, without any included GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded compute capability paired with capable cryptographic acceleration. The instance achieved 18429.89 in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing, 13095.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 46134.8 on the PassMark CPU suite. PassMark CPU encryption placed in the top 25% with 51204.81 points, supported by hardware AES and SHA-NI instruction sets, while the PassMark memory score reached 2888.54. However, single-thread compute shows limitations, marked by a bottom 10% stress-ng single-core score of 765.98, and modern AVX-512 extensions are not supported on this platform.

From an architectural standpoint, the c5ad.12xlarge delivers cost-efficient throughput for workloads that demand significant parallel CPU resources alongside fast temporary disk access. The inclusion of 1.8 TB NVMe storage eliminates external block storage overhead for scratch space, while the 96 GB memory pool is optimal for parallel compute rather than giant in-memory sets. Suitable workloads include distributed batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, video transcoding, and scratch-space-intensive analytics tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz, 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance achieves balanced multi-threaded performance, recording a PassMark CPU score of 46134.8, multi-core Geekbench score of 13095.0, and a top-quartile PassMark encryption score of 51204.81 due to hardware AES acceleration. Single-thread processing registers lower relative metrics, but the system sustains 12 Gbps baseline networking and 43.83 million Redis SET operations per second. With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio and fast attached NVMe disks, c5ad.12xlarge is tailored for parallel data processing, software compilation pipelines, and compute-intensive batch jobs needing high-speed local scratch storage.
